reuse.why: Extends the existing shared helpers (getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getWeekdayOccurrences, getLastWeekdayOccurrence) with a holidays argument instead of adding new paths.

duplication.why: A single isWeekendOrHoliday predicate backs the helpers; no copied blocks, though holidays must be threaded through every call.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts next to the weekend rule; the predicate is private, so server code cannot use it for its own daily check.

scope.why: Only the holiday rule, its plumbing (type, parseRecurDate, callers) and tests.

maintainability.why: Mostly centralised, but getDatesInRange's daily branch still decides 'skip' with its own d.isWeekend check and ignores holidays, and every caller must remember to pass holidays.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange daily branch keeps `if (!d.isWeekend(date))` instead of a shared weekend-or-holiday predicate, so it bypasses the updated rule.

disguised_duplication.where: None added; the remaining inline isWeekend check in getDatesInRange is pre-existing.

one_place.where: Holiday handling lands in shared/schedules.ts (isWeekendOrHoliday via getDateWithSkippedWeekend/getWeekdayOccurrences), but getDatesInRange's daily skip in server/schedules/app.ts still uses its own d.isWeekend check and does not skip holidays.
